rich_summary: After Sita’s abduction, Rama struggles with rage and despair until Lakshmana urges him to search the wild and demon‑haunted region of Janasthana. As they comb the forest, Rama discovers the giant vulture king Jatayu lying bloodied on the ground and initially assumes the bird is a demon who has devoured Sita. Preparing to kill him, Rama is stopped when the dying Jatayu speaks. The vulture reveals that Ravana abducted Sita and that he himself fought the demon king in the sky, smashing his chariot and killing his charioteer before Ravana severed his wings and escaped with Sita. Overcome with grief and gratitude, Rama embraces the dying bird, lamenting his fate and mourning his father’s old friend. The scene is pivotal because it confirms Ravana as Sita’s abductor and frames Jatayu’s heroic resistance as a noble sacrifice.

highlight_spans.why: Opening moment where Lakshmana steadies Rama and urges the search through the wild, mythic landscape of Janasthana.
Jatayu’s revelation that Ravana abducted Sita and that he fought the demon in a desperate aerial battle before his wings were cut off.
Rama embraces the dying Jatayu and laments his misfortune, turning the encounter into a deeply emotional moment of grief and gratitude.

top_scenes.scene_text: Rama and Lakshmana discover the colossal vulture king Jatayu collapsed in the forest, his severed wings and blood staining the earth as Rama approaches with a drawn bow.
In Jatayu’s recollection, the giant bird battles Ravana in the sky, smashing the demon’s chariot and striking with massive wings as Sita struggles in Ravana’s grasp.
Rama kneels in the forest cradling the dying Jatayu in his arms, bow fallen aside, as the heroic bird reveals Sita’s fate under the fading light.
